data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Megen was a warrior goddess. She was known for her strength and courage in battle. Her name comes from the Greek word 'megas,' meaning great or mighty. The name Megen carries the meaning “Strong in war” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Megen usually hope their child will grow to embody strong in war and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Megen belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong in war.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Megen total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Megen may evoke a sense of strength and valor, reminding us of godly redemption and the courage of biblical characters like David, Gideon, and Esther. In modern times, it can be a reminder of the importance of standing up for our faith in a world that may challenge us.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Megen can represent the greatness and might of God. In Isaiah 40:28-29, we read, "Do you not know? Do you not hear? The Lord is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He will not grow tired or weary, and his understanding no one can fathom." God's power and greatness are beyond our comprehension, and the name Megen can serve as a reminder of God's strength and might in our lives. More broadly, the name can serve as a reminder of the greatness of all creation and the importance of recognizing and celebrating the wonder and beauty of God's creation.
